goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:47 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh unrelated TestLogger, so LoggerMiddleware's FromContext(ctx).Info calls are invisible to test assertions and logger tests silently pass while logging is broken.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:79 — NewMetricsMiddleware mutates the shared imw.next on every chain build, so reusing the middleware across multiple clients races and routes all requests to the last-wrapped client.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go, NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single *MetricsMiddleware instance (imw := newMetricsMiddleware(...)) and returns a middleware func that sets imw.next = next and then returns imw. That means each time the returned middleware is applied to wrap a client, it mutates shared state (the same imw.next). If the same middleware value is reused to build multiple client chains (or concurrently), requests will be routed to whichever client was wrapped last and this can race on imw.next.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:88 — Metrics middleware returns ErrPluginNotRegistered before invoking next, so a registry lookup miss makes an observability layer fail the actual plugin request.

adjudication.rationale: In metrics_middleware.go, pluginTarget() returns plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered when the registry lookup misses, and both instrumentPluginRequestSize()/instrumentPluginRequest() propagate that error back to QueryData/CallResource/etc before calling m.next.*. So the middleware can indeed prevent the plugin request from executing on a registry miss. Whether that is a defect is not provable from the diff alone (it may be an intentional guard if unregistered plugins must not be called), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded design/behavior concern for an observability-focused middleware.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:51 — FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the infra logger is not a *ConcreteLogger, dropping all contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, traceID) with no signal.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and then type-asserts to *log.ConcreteLogger; if that fails it returns d.New() with no arguments. That fallback does not incorporate the passed context, so any contextual attributes added to ctx (e.g., via log.WithContextualAttributes in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware) will be omitted from the returned logger with no warning/error, matching the finding’s claim about silently dropping context-derived attributes.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — LoggerMiddleware no longer adds pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID itself and depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware plus a registered infra-log traceID context provider; if either is missing, the "Plugin Request Completed" log loses those fields.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows LoggerMiddleware’s logRequest no longer appends pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID to logParams and now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go). A new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is added and inserted before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)` in `CreateMiddlewares` to enrich the context with endpoint/plugin/user/datasource attributes (contextual_logger_middleware.go, pluginsintegration.go), so in that configured stack those fields should still be present via context. However, this change does create a real coupling/ordering requirement: if LoggerMiddleware is used without ContextualLoggerMiddleware (or if the underlying infra logger doesn’t actually propagate context attributes like traceID), the log will lose those fields. The diff does not prove such a missing stack exists elsewhere, so it’s not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:79 — NewMetricsMiddleware mutates a single shared instance's next field each time the middleware is applied, so wrapping more than one client makes every wrapper forward to the last client, and doing it concurrently is a data race.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go, NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single *MetricsMiddleware instance (imw := newMetricsMiddleware(...)) and returns a ClientMiddlewareFunc closure that mutates imw.next = next and then returns imw. Because the same imw pointer is reused for every application of that middleware, wrapping multiple clients with the returned middleware would cause all wrappers to share and overwrite the same .next field, forwarding to the last wrapped client; concurrent wrapping would also race on .next. This shared-instance mutation is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:103 — pluginTarget failing on an unregistered plugin returns ErrPluginNotRegistered before calling next, so a metrics-only middleware can reject requests.

adjudication.rationale: In `metrics_middleware.go`, `pluginTarget()` returns `plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered` when the plugin is not found in the registry, and both `instrumentPluginRequestSize()` and `instrumentPluginRequest()` propagate that error back to the caller (e.g., `QueryData`), causing the middleware to return early without calling `m.next.*`. After this PR, the middleware is explicitly renamed/split to be metrics-focused, so having it able to reject requests is a real, diff-grounded behavior/architecture concern (even though the lookup/early-return pattern is visible in the new code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:52 — LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being registered earlier to get pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname, creating hidden ordering coupling between middlewares.

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, logRequest no longer adds plugin/request fields itself (removed pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname/traceID from logParams) and instead logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is the one that enriches the context with `endpoint`, `pluginId`, datasource and user attributes via `log.WithContextualAttributes`. CreateMiddlewares registers `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`, so the intended ordering is encoded there, but LoggerMiddleware now implicitly relies on that ordering/context enrichment to preserve prior log fields. If LoggerMiddleware is used without that middleware (or ordering changes), those fields silently disappear. This is a real, diff-grounded coupling/architecture concern, not necessarily a functional defect within the shown wiring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger, so logs emitted via FromContext (as LoggerMiddleware now does) are never recorded in the fake and cannot be asserted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Logger.FromContext(ctx) and updates LoggerMiddleware to log via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` instead of `m.logger.Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go). In the fake implementation, `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` (fake.go), which creates a new logger instance rather than returning `f` or a wrapper around it. As a result, logs emitted through `FromContext` will be recorded on the new instance, not on the original `TestLogger` used by tests, making assertions on `f.InfoLogs`/`f.ErrorLogs` fail or silently miss logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:49 — FromContext type-asserts to concrete *log.ConcreteLogger and silently falls back to d.New() dropping contextual attributes, leaking the infra logger's concrete type into the plugin log boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and type-asserts the result to *log.ConcreteLogger; on failure it silently falls back to d.New() (no context), which would drop any contextual attributes derived from the provided context and ties the wrapper to the infra logger’s concrete type. The diff doesn’t prove this will occur in practice (d.l may always return *log.ConcreteLogger), but the coupling and silent fallback are real, diff-grounded design/edge-case concerns rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:88 — Metrics middleware fails the actual plugin request with ErrPluginNotRegistered when registry lookup misses, so an observability concern can break queries/health checks instead of degrading to an "unknown" target label.

adjudication.rationale: In `metrics_middleware.go`, `pluginTarget()` returns `plugins.ErrPluginNotRegistered` when `m.pluginRegistry.Plugin(ctx, pluginID)` misses, and that error is propagated by both `instrumentPluginRequestSize()` and `instrumentPluginRequest()` before calling `m.next.*` (e.g., `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, `CollectMetrics`). This means metrics instrumentation can block the underlying plugin request when the registry lookup fails. Whether that is a correctness bug is not provable from the diff (it may be intended to fail unregistered plugins), but it is a concrete robustness/architecture concern as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:146 — QueryData/CallResource dereference req without a nil guard (LoggerMiddleware explicitly guards nil req), so a nil request panics here before reaching downstream handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `metrics_middleware.go`, `QueryData` iterates `for _, v := range req.Queries` and uses `req.PluginContext` later; `CallResource` uses `req.PluginContext` and `len(req.Body)`—both will panic if `req` is nil. The diff shows `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly guards `if req == nil { ... }`, but `MetricsMiddleware` sits earlier in the middleware stack (see `CreateMiddlewares`: `NewMetricsMiddleware(...)` before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`), so a nil request would panic in `MetricsMiddleware` before reaching the downstream or LoggerMiddleware handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:79 — Middleware closure mutates a single shared imw.next, so applying the middleware to more than one client silently rewires earlier chains (and races if done concurrently).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go, NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single middleware instance (imw := newMetricsMiddleware(...)) and returns a ClientMiddleware closure that mutates that shared instance via `imw.next = next` before returning `imw`. If the same middleware value is applied to more than one client, the later application overwrites `next` for the earlier one, silently rewiring the chain; and if done concurrently it introduces a data race on `imw.next`. This behavior is directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:58 — MustRegister panics on duplicate registration if CreateMiddlewares/NewMetricsMiddleware is invoked more than once with the same registerer (e.g. tests or re-init).

adjudication.rationale: In `newMetricsMiddleware` (renamed from the prior instrumentation middleware), the code creates new Prometheus collectors with fixed names and calls `promRegisterer.MustRegister(...)`. By Prometheus contract, `MustRegister` will panic if the same `Registerer` already has collectors with those names/desc registered. The diff shows `CreateMiddlewares` constructs this middleware via `NewMetricsMiddleware(promRegisterer, registry)`, so repeated construction with the same `promRegisterer` would be unsafe. However, the diff alone does not prove this happens at runtime (it’s a usage/re-init concern rather than a directly verifiable defect), and the registration pattern appears pre-existing under the old middleware name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:51 — FromContext falls back to d.New() silently when the infra logger is not a *ConcreteLogger, dropping all contextual attributes (pluginId, endpoint, traceID) with no signal.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) does `concreteInfraLogger, ok := d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and if the type assertion fails it returns `d.New()` with no args. That fallback is silent and does not use `ctx`, so any contextual attributes that were meant to be derived from the request context will be lost in that path. However, whether this is a true defect depends on whether `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` can realistically return a non-*log.ConcreteLogger in this codebase; the diff alone can’t prove it happens in practice (and the mention of traceID specifically isn’t supported here since traceID logging was removed from LoggerMiddleware).
